title: A Fully Differentiable Neuro-Soft-Symbolic Framework for Perceptual Task Planning
abstract: arXiv:2609.21221v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Perceptual planning tasks require two key capabilities: accurately perceiving uncertain scenes and planning valid action sequences following logical rules. Conventional methods convert perception into discrete symbolic facts and then plan, discarding perceptual uncertainty and severing task-level feedback to perception. We introduce a generic, fully differentiable neuro-soft-symbolic framework that connects visual perception and task planning within a single computational graph. The framework maintains a continuous soft symbolic state, lifts domain rules into a differentiable soft-$T_P$ transition operator, and optimizes action logits over a short planning horizon. Gradients from the planning objective can also update the perception parameters, allowing task-relevant perceptual representations to be refined during planning. On Blocksworld, our method solves 40/40 LatPlan-40 tasks and 596/600 PlanBench-600 tasks, compared with 33/40 for L

translated_title: 一种用于感知任务规划的全可微神经-软-符号框架
translated_abstract: 感知规划任务需要两项关键能力：准确感知不确定的场景，以及遵循逻辑规则规划有效的动作序列。传统方法先将感知结果转换为离散的符号事实再进行规划，这丢弃了感知的不确定性，并切断了任务层面对感知的反馈。我们提出了一个通用的、完全可微的神经-软-符号框架，将视觉感知与任务规划连接在单一计算图之中。该框架维护一个连续的软符号状态，将领域规则提升为可微的软-$T_P$转移算子，并在短规划时域内优化动作logits。来自规划目标的梯度还可以用于更新感知参数，使与任务相关的感知表示能够在规划过程中不断被优化。在Blocksworld上，我们的方法解决了40/40个LatPlan-40任务和596/600个PlanBench-600任务，而对比方法仅为33/40。
tldr: 该论文提出一个全可微的神经-软-符号框架，在单一计算图中连接视觉感知与任务规划，使规划目标的梯度能够反向优化感知参数，从而在Blocksworld等基准上显著提升了感知任务规划的成功率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a fully differentiable neuro-soft-symbolic framework that connects visual perception and task planning within a single computational graph, allowing planning gradients to refine perception parameters and achieving substantially higher success rates on Blocksworld perceptual planning benchmarks.
